newsitem.title: JAPAN: OLYMPICS-NAGANO MEDIA CHIEF SAYS SUPPORT GROWING.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPICS-NAGANO MEDIA CHIEF SAYS SUPPORT GROWING.

text.p: Although there are few outward signs of it yet, the new media chief for next year's Winter Olympics said on Thursday that interest in the Games is picking up.
"Gradually the Nagano presence will grow," said Ko Yamaguchi, who took over last month as head of media for the Games.
He replaces Akira Hashimoto, who officials said stepped down for health reasons.

Earlier this year, the Nagano organisers were criticised by International Olympic Committee president Juan Antonio Samaranch for not doing enough to promote the Games, which will be held next February 7-22.
Japanese Olympic officials have also criticised Nagano's lagging media operations.
"We will beef up our public relations," Yamaguchi said. "The Nagano people are in high spirits, but we have to get the message to Tokyo."
Yamaguchi said ticket sales in Japan were "quite good, better than expected".
Tickets for events such as the opening ceremony, figure skating and ice hockey sold out within minutes of going on sale in Japan earlier this month.
Yamaguchi, 53, is a former bureau chief in Geneva for the Japanese news agency Kyodo, and was a war correspondent in Vietnam.
